items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: Because he had played with Bix Beiderbecke in the Jean Goldkette Orchestra.

ctx.x: Yeah. Were you developing, by the time you were in your teens and so forth, any kind of personal filter — oh I really want to play this kind of music and I don’t care for this kind of music too much. Or was it just like a gig is a gig?

No it wasn’t quite like that. You see because of what I told you was on that table, there was the Salt City Five, which was Dixieland, then Eddie Condon’s music called “Jam Session Coast to Coast,” which had the Rampart Street Paraders on one side with Nick Fatool, a great drummer, and on the other side was the Condon band, which was just dynamite, with Wild Bill Davison and all those guys. And then there was a big band. So like I was in between — and like Ellington “Uptown” and I was right in between. So I had…
quartet was with Hamp. So I started playing that music. So I mean it was all subsumed. It was subsumed as just being jazz.
